statement: The supplied source contains no derivation (the log-odds update derivation and recursive substitution are absent from the source). Occupancy grid mapping defines a map $m$ as an evenly spaced grid of binary random variables $m_i$ representing obstacle presence at locations in continuous space, approximating the joint posterior probability over maps given sensor measurements $z_{1:t}$ and known robot poses $x_{1:t}$ by the factored product of marginal grid cell probabilities: $p(m \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t}) = \prod_{i} p(m_i \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t})$.

properties.property: The full map posterior is approximated by factoring into a product of individual cell posteriors: p(m \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t}) = \prod_{i} p(m_i \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t})
properties.why: Breaks down a computationally intractable 2^{N} dimensional estimation problem into N separate binary estimation problems

properties.property: A binary Bayes filter can be used to estimate the occupancy probability for each individual grid cell
properties.why: The factorization decomposes the estimation problem into independent binary problems

properties.property: Occupancy probabilities for each cell are commonly maintained in a log-odds representation
properties.why: It is a standard representation used in conjunction with binary Bayes filters for estimating cell occupancy

properties.property: Dependencies between neighboring cells are not modeled
properties.why: The independent cell breakdown loses spatial correlation structure in exchange for tractability

properties.property: Controls and odometry data play no part in the mapping algorithm
properties.why: The robot path x_{1:t} is assumed to be known

assumptions.assumption: The robot pose trajectory x_{1:t} is known exactly
assumptions.breaks_when: Robot localization is noisy, uncertain, or unobserved, requiring controls and odometry to estimate poses jointly with the map

assumptions.assumption: The joint map posterior can be factored into a product of independent marginal cell posteriors
assumptions.breaks_when: Dependencies and correlations between neighboring cells are significant and cannot be neglected

assumptions.assumption: The environment is discretized into an evenly spaced field of binary static cells
assumptions.breaks_when: The environment contains dynamic moving obstacles or continuous/multi-state occupancy characteristics

failure_modes.signature: Inability to model spatial relationships and correlations across adjacent cells
failure_modes.cause: Approximating the joint posterior p(m \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t}) by the independent product factorization \prod_i p(m_i \mid z_{1:t}, x_{1:t})

failure_modes.signature: Computational infeasibility with 2^{N} possible map states (e.g., 2^{10,000} for 10,000 cells)
failure_modes.cause: Attempting to compute the full posterior over all map configurations directly without factoring into individual cells

failure_modes.mode: Map inconsistency due to localization error
failure_modes.signature: Distorted, blurry, or duplicated obstacles in the generated map
failure_modes.cause: Violation of the assumption that robot path and poses x_{1:t} are known exactly
